instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in a few changes of water until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a pot with 1 3/4 cups water, bring it to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered while you cook the shrimp.

Trim the green beans and cut them in half. Mince the 4 garlic cloves and enough ginger to fill 2 tsp. Slice the 3 green onions. Pat the shrimp dry and toss them with the salt. In a small bowl, stir together the 2 tbsp soy sauce and the 1 tbsp gochujang.

Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large skillet over high heat. Add the green beans and cook for 3 minutes, until they blister in spots. Add 2 tbsp water, cover, and cook for 2 minutes, until tender but still crisp. Move them to a plate.

Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the skillet. Lay the shrimp in a single layer and leave them for 1 minute, until the undersides turn pink. Flip them, add the garlic and ginger, and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in the soy and gochujang mixture, add the green beans back, and toss for 1 minute, until the shrimp are pink, curled and opaque all the way through.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the sesame oil, sesame seeds and green onions.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: No version of this dish had 20 ratings, and two of the three read have none at all. Evolution of Flavour builds it on garlic, ginger, gochujang and soy with green beans, so it leads. Hanna-One cooks the shrimp with broccoli, carrot and zucchini in a blended ginger and garlic paste with fish sauce; Voko marinates the shrimp in a sweeter gochujang and honey sauce for 20 minutes. This follows the lead but cooks the green beans first so the shrimp only spend about 3 minutes in the pan, and uses 4 cloves of garlic, where the lead uses 3 and Hanna-One uses 6.
